target_customer: Businesses in Saudi Arabia that need warehousing and transport, from SMEs to large firms and government bodies
problem: Warehouse space in Saudi Arabia was hard to get quickly and on flexible terms; Sirdab says demand exceeded supply by 30 to 50 percent.
business_model: Warehousing as a service with month to month, 6 month and 12 month contracts, plus transport and WMS and OMS software

founders.name: Naif Alzahri
founders.background_notes: Listed on the YC page; no background found.

founders.name: Abdulrahman Alnamlah
founders.background_notes: Listed on the YC page and the BECO Capital page; no background found.

technical_complexity.rationale: A marketplace and software layer over leased and partner warehouses; the hard parts are operations and supply, not technology.

defensibility.rationale: A network of over 50 warehouses in 8 Saudi cities, per the YC page, and WMS and OMS integration give some lock in, though space can be rented elsewhere.

takeover_risk_then.outcome: No acquisition found; Sirdab raised its own Series A in September 2026.

market_need_then: Sirdab cites demand above warehouse supply by 30 to 50 percent in Saudi Arabia; a Knight Frank item in search results noted warehouse occupancy nearing saturation (later date, not opened).

identity.voice_and_tone: Confident and professional, claiming Saudi Arabia's number one logistics network

branding.community_and_virality: No community evidence; some outlets misspell it as Sardab. Press coverage in Inc. Arabia (December 2023) and Wamda.

brand_strength.rationale: A regional word brand with local press and big named clients, but no evidence about the name itself driving growth.

outcome_analysis: Sirdab grew from a cloud warehousing startup in the Winter 2023 batch into a broader logistics platform and in September 2026 raised a 10 million dollar Series A co-led by Elm and BECO Capital to expand across the GCC. It claims 20x revenue growth since the batch and profitability, which are company figures. A local market with supply gaps and large named clients supports its traction.
notes: Series A of SAR 37.5M (about $10M) reported by Wamda and Sharikat Mubasher in September 2026. A $500K pre-seed dated April 2023 appears only on aggregators (Dealroom style listings, FundedIQ), so not recorded. Coverage partial because seed rounds are not itemised. Dealroom says founded 2021, YC and CB Insights say 2022. The word sirdab is an Arabic word for cellar, but no company source gives the name origin, so it is not recorded. Regional competitors found (Khazenly, SideUp, UNITS, Salasa, Logexa) appeared on undated pages, so none are listed. Founder backgrounds not found.
